title: Glassy dynamics with softened kinetic constraints on a noisy quantum computer
authors: Marcel Cech, Igor Lesanovsky, Federico Carollo
abstract: Mid-circuit measurements provide direct access to trajectory-level observables, revealing dynamical structures in many-body systems that are invisible in ensemble-averaged quantities. We exploit this capability to realize and study an instance of the Floquet-East model on a superconducting quantum processor. Here, the combination of mid-circuit measurements, kinetically constrained unitary operations and hardware noise gives rise to intricate many-body phenomena. Analyzing trajectories obtained from temporally and spatially resolved mid-circuit measurements, we identify dynamical heterogeneity --- a hallmark of glassy dynamics. We quantify this emergent behavior by studying the probability of finding inactive space-time regions of a given size. This quantity displays a crossover from an area- to perimeter-dominated scaling, which is a characteristic property of glasses and is associated with the proximity to a dynamical first-order phase transition. Our results establish current noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices as scalable testbeds for investigating correlated many-body phenomena at the level of measurement trajectories.
summary: This paper investigates glassy dynamics in a quantum system using mid-circuit measurements on a superconducting quantum processor. By analyzing the statistics of 'inactive' measurement regions, the authors quantify dynamical heterogeneity. They find a characteristic area-to-perimeter scaling crossover, confirming the system's proximity to a dynamical first-order phase transition using current NISQ devices.
main_problem: The study investigates glassy dynamics in many-body systems by analyzing quantum measurement trajectories, revealing structures invisible in ensemble averages.
main_result: The analysis identifies dynamical heterogeneity, characterized by a crossover in the scaling of inactive cluster probabilities from area-law to perimeter-law, suggesting proximity to a dynamical first-order phase transition.
method: The authors analyze quantum trajectories obtained from mid-circuit measurements on a superconducting quantum processor, using thermodynamic analogies to define a dynamical free energy from the probability of inactive space-time regions.
model_or_system: The study employs the Floquet-East model, implemented on a superconducting quantum processor (ibm kingston). The dynamics are complicated by hardware noise, which effectively softens the underlying kinetic constraints.
key_observables: Dynamical heterogeneity, the probability of finding inactive space-time regions ($p_{\ell 	imes 	au}$), and the resulting dynamical free energy ($F_{\ell 	imes 	au}$).
important_parameters: The crossover point in scaling behavior, the effective bit-flip probability ($p_{	ext{flip}}$), and the system size parameters ($\ell, 	au$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that hardware noise can be modeled as independent bit-flips, effectively softening the kinetic constraints, and that the system's behavior is dominated by the statistics of inactive clusters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate circuit implementations, exemplary quantum trajectories showing inactive clusters, and plots comparing the scaling of the negative log-probability ($F_{\ell 	imes 	au}$) versus temporal extensions ($	au$), showing the characteristic crossover.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical model and measurement setup, then developing the theoretical framework using cluster probabilities and free energy, and finally applying this analysis to both the classical deterministic limit and the noisy quantum regime to extract scaling signatures.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum computation hardware limitations (noise) with fundamental condensed matter concepts (glassy dynamics, phase transitions) by analyzing measurement-level observables, providing a novel experimental testbed.
